text:
maria (Platform PM): Heads-up: SI partner asked if we can ship certified marketplace images this week. We found a regression on CUDA12.3.0 in our perf sweep. Need alignment on pin vs. rollback + messaging.

nate (Eng-Platform): Summary: CUDA12.3.0 increases p95 by ~12% on 7B-ish autoregressive runs (seq=2048). ROCm5.9 shows stable perf but a slight jitter on startup. Error logs point to a new kernel memory-copy path for large KV caches.

olga (SI): Our customer's compliance timeline is tight. If you recommend pinning to 12.2, can we get an image signed/certified today? They can't tolerate a surprise perf regression.

ashok (AMD): From AMD side (hi), ROCm5.9 has an outstanding memcpy optimization that landed in our internal branch; public CI artifacts pending. If you want a ROCm-only certified option, we can prioritize 24hr validation.

cheng (NVIDIA): Cheng here. We're tracking a regress in cuBLAS/cuDNN interplay for large batch GEMM shapes. We expect a micro-patch within 48 hours and a full validated driver build in ~5 business days. Can you share the failing perf harness config?

nate (Eng-Platform): Repro gist: model=llama-ish-7B, batch=1, seq=2048, kv-shard=2. Command: ```python perf_harness.py --model llama-7b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --kv-shards 2``` Also attaching kernel symbols we saw in logs (short).

maria (Platform PM): Options on the table: A) Pin marketplace images to CUDA=12.2 and ROCm=5.9, mark 12.3 experimental; B) Ship 12.3 and provide runtime fallback/override; C) Delay certified image until NVIDIA patch. Thoughts?

olga (SI): A is safest for our customer. They need determinism. If you can produce a signed 12.2 image today, we'll proceed. B is risky unless fallback is automatic and transparent.

raj (Marketplace): We can produce a signed 12.2 tile today if Eng signs off. We will add an "experimental: cuda-12.3" tag and a clear note: "Performance regression observed on certain transformer workloads; use for testing only."

market-bot: CI job #tile-922 completed: marketplace-image-cuda12.2: signing OK, vuln-scan passed.

nate (Eng-Platform): Runtime fallback status: we can ship a kernel-override shim that redirects to older blas kernel on matching op shapes in ~36 hours. It requires a quick hotfix rollout in runtime and smoke validation. Less risky than delaying certification.

cheng (NVIDIA): If fallback is used, we recommend documenting exact op shapes so customers know the mitigation is per-op. We'll coordinate to ensure the patched driver doesn't clash with the override.

ashok (AMD): If you plan to present ROCm as an alternative, we can expedite a ROCm5.9 validated artifact in 24-36 hours for SI certification. Caveat: some cloud partners may need additional signing.

maria (Platform PM): Proposed final plan: 1) Produce certified marketplace image pinned to CUDA12.2 + ROCm5.9 today (raj). 2) Publish experimental CUDA12.3 tile labeled clearly as preview/testing (raj). 3) Nate -> prepare runtime kernel-override hotfix PR (target 36h) for partners wanting 12.3 while NVIDIA patches. 4) Cheng -> deliver patch candidate in 48h and validated driver in 5 business days. 5) Olga -> confirm customer's go-ahead for pinned image.

olga (SI): Confirmed: customer will accept pinned 12.2 image today. Please include a short "what changed" note and contact for hotfixes.

nate (Eng-Platform): Will open PR: runtime/kernel-override + tests, and mark canary image tag. I'll post links once CI runs.

raj (Marketplace): I'll update marketplace tile copy: short blurb "Pinned to CUDA12.2 due to observed perf regression in CUDA12.3 on large transformer KV workloads. Experimental CUDA12.3 available for testing. Contact partnerships@ for hotfixes."

cheng (NVIDIA): We'll run your harness with our internal patch and share kernel diffs. If the patch is green, we'll push a signed driver build.

market-bot: Release note created: release/marketplace-cuda12.2-signed (ID: rn-214540A).

maria (Platform PM): Good alignment. Two additional asks: - Legal needs a short risk blurb for SI contracts (lee will draft) - DevEx wants the perf-eval set so SIs can validate (anya will post).

ashok (AMD): Looping in our CI contact to help with validation for ROCm artifacts.

nate (Eng-Platform): Quick caveat: kernel-override will change the kernel selection table; expect a small risk window during canary. We'll label canary "runtime-fallback-enabled" and keep it off for default certified tile.

olga (SI): Thanks — that addresses our customer's timeline. Please DM me the cert package link when ready.

maria (Platform PM): Closing thread: raj -> publish pinned tile, nate -> PR in 36h, cheng -> patch in 48h, ashok -> ROCm help, olga -> confirm receipt. Reopen if blockers. :thumbsup:
